sources.title: Museum of the Bosnian Kingdom: Economic rise
sources.note: Fourteenth- and fifteenth-century mining, carriers, merchant colonies and urban markets; broad origin claims and national teleology are not adopted.

sources.title: UNESCO: Stećci Medieval Tombstone Graveyards
sources.note: Twelfth- to sixteenth-century chronology, strongest production in fourteenth to fifteenth centuries; limestone, varied forms and use across three Christian communities.

sources.title: National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Mirko Radojević’s funerary shroud
sources.note: Kopošići excavation in 2015, grave dated to the fifteenth century, oak coffin, purple brocade, gilded-silver threads; named attribution is the museum’s interpretation.

sources.title: Museum of the Bosnian Kingdom: Ključ on the Sana
sources.note: Last king’s capture and execution in 1463; subsequent Hungarian action and changing control; castle layout adapted to terrain.

sources.title: History Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Catalogue of medieval coins
sources.note: Printed pages 98 to 99, catalogue items 4 to 5: Tvrtko II groš, dimensions, coat of arms and Latin legend.

sources.title: Museum of the Bosnian Kingdom: Boljuni
sources.note: Necropolis, livestock and caravan economy, inscriptions naming stoneworkers and scribes.

sources.title: Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Austro-Hungarian rule
sources.note: Occupation in 1878, annexation in 1908, statute and Council in 1910, imperial abolition of Council in 1915; constitutional limits.

sources.title: Parliamentary Assembly: Political representation, 1918 to 1941
sources.note: Transfer of authority in 1918 and incorporation into the new South Slav kingdom; no claim that the modern state was founded then.

sources.title: Parliamentary Assembly: Monograph, English edition
sources.note: Austro-Hungarian section reproduces the 1910 title page: Zemaljski ustav (statut) za Bosnu i Hercegovinu; original Latin-script wording, not an invented phrase.

sources.title: Railways of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina: History
sources.note: Narrow-gauge railway construction after 1878, improvised passenger cars with cloth roofs and curtains; construction milestones.

sources.title: National Museum: Library
sources.note: Library operating in 1888, curators’ responsibilities, specialist librarian Franjo Topič in 1898 to 1913, new buildings in 1913.

sources.title: National Museum: Sarajevo Haggadah
sources.note: Purchase from the Koen family in 1894; manuscript’s family Seder setting, parchment and Hebrew text. Earlier Spanish origin is distinct from Sarajevo acquisition.

sources.title: Sarajevo Museum: Despić House
sources.note: Wealthy Orthodox merchant household, building phases and private theatre; an elite example, not a universal home.

sources.title: Žanka Dodig Karaman: The Despić House
sources.note: Summary, printed page 50: performances entertained guests; Makso Despić was an Ottoman treasurer and later Austro-Hungarian city councillor.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum: Hungary under the Treaty of Trianon
sources.note: 1920 to 1938 room: Horthy regency, depression, Art Deco reading interior and 1928 honorary certificate. Nationalist evaluative wording is not adopted.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum: Rise and fall of communism
sources.note: Coercive collectivization, 1956 statue fragment, reconstructed interiors, 1989 border wire and 1990 transition.

sources.title: US Holocaust Memorial Museum: Deportation of Hungarian Jews
sources.note: May to July 1944 deportations by Hungarian gendarmerie under German SS guidance, and murder of the majority deported to Auschwitz.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: Albert Szent-Györgyi biography
sources.note: Szeged research, paprika as a vitamin C source and biological oxidation; priority claims about other discoveries are not adopted.

sources.title: UNESCO: Táncház teaching method
sources.note: 2011 safeguarding record: direct observation, live music, individual creativity, singing, crafts and ethnographic teaching.

sources.title: National Legislation Database: Fundamental Law of Hungary
sources.note: 2011 Fundamental Law, Foundation Article B(1): Magyarország független, demokratikus jogállam. A legal declaration, not an assessment of implementation.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum: In defence of my client
sources.note: Community-loaned objects, Hoffmann typewriter and family photograph circa 1953; persecution and forced relocation in the 1950s.

sources.title: European Central Bank: New EU Member States, 2004
sources.note: Contemporaneous 30 April 2004 announcement of Hungary’s accession on 1 May.

sources.title: National History Museum of Romania: Union of the Principalities
sources.note: Cuza’s election in Moldavia and Wallachia in January 1859; union distinguishes the later Romanian state from the medieval principalities.

sources.title: Bucharest Municipality Museum: Money in Mircea the Elder’s time
sources.note: Ducat and ban issues, continued older coins, international circulation, trade and military payments; celebratory generalizations avoided.

sources.title: CIMEC: Wallachian trade with Brașov, fourteenth to sixteenth centuries
sources.note: Routes, merchandise, craftsmen and market towns. The page’s inconsistent date for account statistics is not used.

sources.title: National Archaeological Register: Cozia Monastery
sources.note: RAN 167927.01: foundation in the later 1380s, inauguration charter in 1388 and interior painting dated 1390 to 1391.

sources.title: CIMEC: Holy Trinity Church, Cozia
sources.note: Window surrounds, carved rosettes and early narthex painting; 1517 renewal and fountain. Inconsistent exact construction range is avoided.

sources.title: Cercetări Numismatice: X-ray analysis of Mircea’s coinage
sources.note: Study of 66 pre-reform coins in the Hungarian National Museum, with hoard histories and uncertain provenances carefully identified.

sources.title: CIMEC: Neacșu’s letter, text
sources.note: 1521 letter as a scholarly Latin-letter transcription of its Cyrillic original; Romanian body, Slavonic formulas, opening report and secrecy request.

sources.title: Dan Alexe: Transcribing Cyrillic names and words
sources.note: Original linguistic commentary, paragraph beginning Primul monument: Cyrillic rendering Ипак дау щире; compared with the CIMEC historical transcription. Unrelated commentary is not adopted.

sources.title: CIMEC: The letter of Neacșu
sources.note: Câmpulung, 1521, warning to Johannes Benkner of Brașov; later than the atlas interval. Do not repeat the outdated absolute earliest-text claim.

sources.title: National History Museum: Back to school, back to the museum
sources.note: Casa Școalelor founded in 1896, funding school construction; 1927 to 1930 school medal and 1947 designs of pupils and weaving.

sources.title: National Museum of Art of Romania: Palace and museum history
sources.note: Carol I as king from 1881; forced abdication in 1947, nationalization in 1948, museum use and damage during the 1989 events.

sources.title: National History Museum: Institutional and building history
sources.note: Postal Palace construction in 1894 to 1899, inauguration in 1901, architect Alexandru Săvulescu and allegorical sculpture.

sources.title: National History Museum: Philatelic collection
sources.note: Postage-due stamps, first Romanian issue on 1 May 1881, six denominations printed at the Bucharest stamp factory.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditional wall-carpet craftsmanship exhibition
sources.note: 2024 exhibition: wall insulation, later decorative functions and regional variation. Unsubstantiated millennia-long continuity language is not repeated.

sources.title: UNESCO: Cultural practices associated with 1 March
sources.note: 2017 multinational inscription: red-white threads, gift exchange, seasonal signs and learning from older people and workshops; origin claims avoided.

sources.title: US Holocaust Memorial Museum: Romania
sources.note: Antonescu regime and Romanian participation in persecution and murder; no collective responsibility assigned to all Romanians.

sources.title: Romanian Senate: Constitution of 1991
sources.note: Article 1, adoption in November 1991, republican government and stated rights.

sources.title: Serbian National Assembly: History, 1804 to 1918
sources.note: Constitutions of 1888 and 1903, assembly meeting places, wartime sessions and withdrawal in 1915.

sources.title: National Bank of Serbia: History of money
sources.note: Recognition in 1878, gold coins in 1879, banknotes in 1884, foreign printing, 1918 unification, 2003 institutional renaming and 2006 continuity.

sources.title: National Bank of Serbia: Founding the national bank
sources.note: Kingdom proclaimed in 1882, founding law in 1883, bank operations from July 1884.

sources.title: National Bank of Serbia: Publications about the bank
sources.note: Bibliographical entry for the 1909 book Привилегована Народна банка Краљевине Србије: 1884 to 1909, publisher St. Ljub. M. Davidović, Belgrade.

sources.title: Belgrade Cultural Heritage Preservation Institute: Knez Mihailova Street area
sources.note: English pages 8 to 9: wells and Delijska Fountain before 1892 water system, electric lighting in 1891, mixed commercial/residential houses and architectural changes.

sources.title: Serbian Academy Mathematical Institute: The Serbian school of mathematics
sources.note: Printed page 72: Milanković appointed in 1909, shared office, theoretical/applied teaching and Berić’s first Belgrade mathematics doctorate in 1912.

sources.title: Serbian Academy: Mihailo Petrović Alas catalogue
sources.note: Printed page 133: hydro-integrator built in 1900 and bronze medal at the Paris exhibition; scientific activity timeline.

sources.title: International Review of the Red Cross: Florence Nightingale medal recipient notice
sources.note: Printed page 347, recipient 11: Ljubica Luković’s nursing service, care for enemy wounded and death during the 1915 typhus epidemic at Valjevo.

sources.title: National Museum of Serbia: Museum history
sources.note: Foundation in 1844 as prior context and later museum development; specific collecting purpose rather than general national claims.

sources.title: United Nations: Yugoslavia and successor states
sources.note: FR Yugoslavia’s UN admission in 2000, Serbia and Montenegro name in 2003, Montenegro’s independence and Serbian membership continuity in 2006.

sources.title: UNESCO: Zlakusa pottery making
sources.note: 2020 inscription: clay and calcite, hand wheel, seven-to-ten-day process, practical vessels, demonstrations and apprenticeship.

sources.title: UNESCO: Slava, family patron saint’s celebration
sources.note: 2014 record of Orthodox family ritual, cake, wine, relatives and guests; women’s role in transmission. Not every Serbian family practices it.

sources.title: National Bank of Serbia: Decision on the 100-dinar banknote
sources.note: 2003 issue, sections 4 to 6: Cyrillic and Latin bank names, Nikola Tesla imagery, electromagnetic engine, infrared and ultraviolet security features.

sources.title: UNICEF: Climate landscape analysis and children in Serbia
sources.note: Access to basic services section: 2014 floods, school damage, temporary shelter and healthcare interruption.

sources.title: United Nations: Report S/1999/662
sources.note: Paragraphs 13 to 15 and subsequent sections: fighting, civilian displacement and NATO air strikes from March 1999.

sources.title: International Court of Justice: Kosovo advisory opinion overview
sources.note: Declaration in 2008, 2010 advisory opinion on the declaration’s lawfulness; this was not a universal recognition ruling.

sources.title: Government of Serbia: Constitution of 2006
sources.note: Adoption, referendum and proclamation in 2006; constitutional institutions and language. Territorial assertions are distinguished from international recognition.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Benedictine Abbey of Pannonhalma
sources.note: Brief synthesis: foundation in 996, successive churches, 1224 building phase, Porta Speciosa and 1486 cloister. The introductory description of the 1055 document as entirely Hungarian is not adopted.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum, Arpadian period
sources.note: Opening chronology 1000-1301; centaur aquamanile and Beszterec vessel catalogue entries. Imported objects are not described as Hungarian inventions. Conflicting discovery years in the Monomachus entry are not used.

sources.title: Endre Toth, The Coronation Mantle, Hungarian National Museum
sources.note: 2023 publication description: Stephen and Gisela donated the chasuble in 1031 to the Szekesfehervar basilica; its later use as coronation regalia is a separate phase.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum, Villages and towns in the late fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries
sources.note: Introduction and Fun facts on heating and hand-painted printed missals; Bothar workshop stove-tile caption and spectacle frame from Liptoszentandras, before 1470. A find behind an altar is not evidence of a named user.

sources.title: National Szechenyi Library, The Corvina Library and the Buda Workshop
sources.note: Curator Edina Zsupan, 2018 exhibition: The Buda workshop, Achievements and Decorative codices of high priests. Ranzano manuscript reassessment and late-reign uniform binding. Estimated library size is not used.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum, Ottoman period
sources.note: Nyirbator choir-stall entry: 1511 patron inscription, F. Marone maker mark and inlaid cabinets with books and kitchen utensils. The object predates Ottoman occupation despite its exhibition-room heading.

sources.title: Marta Pallag, Mohacs as a place of national memory, Hungarian National Museum
sources.note: Opening account: battle on 29 August 1526 and death of Louis II; medals as retrospective imperial representations, not neutral eyewitness illustrations.

sources.title: Karoly Magyar, Ottoman-era Buda, Research Centre for the Humanities
sources.note: Page 1, Mohacs utan - Buda elfoglalasa elott: rival kings after 1526; Ottoman withdrawals before permanent occupation in 1541. Do not collapse the stages into a single instant conquest of Hungary.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum, Transylvania and Royal Hungary
sources.note: Opening account of internally autonomous Ottoman-vassal Transylvania, Habsburg kings, mining, guilds and Hutterite craft. Broad claims about religious freedom or population percentages are not adopted.

sources.title: Hungarian National Museum: Coronation Mantle
sources.note: Opening embroidered dedication: A STEPHANO REGE ET GISLA REGINA; 1031 original chasuble, later converted into a coronation mantle. This is earlier evidence, not a 1492–1530 inscription.
